chapter_title: 第73章 徐有漁的親自邀請

segments.title: 第73章 徐有漁的親自邀請
segments.content:
Chapter 73: Xu Youyu's Personal Invitation

In an empty classroom on the sixth floor of the Year Two academic building.

Duan Qintian, the president of the Literature Club, looked at today's club recruitment list.

Generally speaking, most students in their first year would pick a subject they were interested in to join a competition club, and then pick a hobby-based club they liked.

Unless a student was particularly artistic, held a certain romanticized view of literature, and enjoyed reading and writing in their spare time, very few would sign up for the Literature Club.

Therefore, the Literature Club was neither like the Math Club or Physics Club, which had competition teachers giving separate lessons every day, nor was it like major clubs such as the Basketball Club or Anime Club, which had a huge number of members.

Last year, for instance, only about fifty or so students joined the Literature Club, and more than half of them were students who had previously won major composition awards or received a perfect score on their high school entrance exam essay.

The number was about the same this year, just over fifty, but with one exception: a student with a perfect score on his entrance exam essay not only didn't show up for recruitment but also rejected the vice president's personal invitation.

"This kid, Li Luo, has a terrible attitude." Qin Yawei couldn't help but complain the moment she entered the classroom. "I hadn't even said anything, and he just flat out refused."

"I even told him that he only needs to submit one manuscript a month and doesn't have to do anything else."

"Our Literature Club isn't like those competition clubs that have classes all the time and mini-tests on weekends. It's such a relaxed club, and he still won't join."

"Alright, alright." Duan Qintian waved his hand. "This has happened before. Maybe he's just not interested."

He said that, but of the 37-person list given by the teacher, both Duan Qintian and Xu Youyu had successfully recruited all the students they were responsible for. Only Qin Yawei had missed one, Li Luo, so she was certainly unhappy.

"You just said, what was the name of the student who wouldn't join?" Xu Youyu asked curiously.

"Li Luo. Why?"

"The class president of Year One, Class Eight?"

"I don't know if he's the class president, but he is in Class Eight."

"Oh, I see." Xu Youyu chuckled, finding it rather interesting.

She hadn't expected Li Luo to refuse so directly, though.

"Do you know this student?" Duan Qintian couldn't help but ask, seeing her reaction.

"I guess you could say that."

"Then could I trouble you to go and ask him again tomorrow in Qin Yawei's place?" Duan Qintian was quite confident in Xu Youyu's charm.

As long as Xu Youyu was willing to make a move, and the other party was a boy, it was basically a done deal.

Hearing this, Qin Yawei, who was standing nearby, immediately frowned and looked like she wanted to say something.

But she glanced at Xu Youyu's full chest and delicate side profile, then just huffed and remained silent.

That Li Luo kid had better stand his ground.

If he joined the moment Xu Youyu invited him, Qin Yawei would definitely look down on him—just another ordinary, vulgar boy.

"Alright, I'll give it a try," Xu Youyu said with a nod. "But I can't guarantee it'll work."

"It's fine. If he really doesn't want to join, we won't force him," Duan Qintian said. "If there's nothing else, let's wrap it up. Xu Youyu still has to get home, right?"

"Mhm." Xu Youyu stood up and stretched, already longing for Li Luo's fried noodles. "I'll be going then, bye-bye."

Walking home, Xu Youyu breathed in the fresh night air, her steps light as she thought about Li Luo's fried noodles.

Actually, if she wanted to, she could move back into the staff residence building of Qianjiang University next door, and her mother would make her late-night snacks.

But compared to the comfort of home, Xu Youyu yearned for the feeling of freedom.

Her family was a standard scholarly one. She had a strict upbringing and was steeped in traditional literature from a young age, making her a perfectly well-behaved girl in her childhood.

It was only later, when she accidentally came across webnovels and discovered another side of literature she never knew, that her personality gradually began to change.

Then Xu Youyu discovered that while traditional literary classics were good, the characters and hardships within them always prompted contemplation and melancholy with every reading.

But reading webnovels brought absolute and pure joy.

If traditional literature was a sharp sword piercing the hazy veil of reality, then webnovels were the wings that fulfilled fantastical dreams.

It was just that in her father's eyes, so-called webnovels were ultimately nothing more than a kind of low-brow literary garbage.

If he found out his own daughter was writing this stuff, Xu Youyu dared not imagine the scene.

Back when she wanted to sign a contract, Xu Youyu had secretly taken the household registration book from home to make a copy, played two roles to fool the editor, and then signed the contract using the photocopy.

And to avoid being discovered while writing, she had started laying the groundwork back in her first year of high school, saying that she needed to learn to be independent now that she was in high school and applying to rent a place to live.

Since the rented apartment was right across from Qianjiang University anyway, her parents agreed.

As for the school's Literature Club, it was a way to satisfy her parents' expectations, so Xu Youyu had always participated seriously.

Thinking of this, Xu Youyu found it amusing. She knew very well why Li Luo didn't want to join the Literature Club.

After all, with that kind of time, one might as well write a few more chapters.

"Mmm... it smells so good." When Xu Youyu returned to Apartment 1502, the aroma of fried noodles wafted over from the kitchen the moment she opened the door. She eagerly swapped into her slippers and pattered over.

She poked her head into the kitchen and saw Li Luo stir-frying. She asked, "Where's Xixi?"

"She went to take a shower," Li Luo replied. "The fried noodles will be ready in a moment."

"Okay," Xu Youyu answered. She first went to her bedroom to put down her schoolbag and turn on her computer, then returned to the kitchen, took a packet of fruit powder from the fridge, and made three glasses of juice.

By this time, Li Luo's fried noodles were ready.

He served a bowl for himself and one for Xu Youyu, leaving Ying Chanxi's portion in the wok with the lid on to keep it from getting cold in case her shower took too long.

Nearby, Xu Youyu placed the juice on the dining table. Seeing Li Luo come out with the plates, she asked with a smile, "Which club did you end up choosing at the recruitment today?"

"The Basketball Club, of course," Li Luo said as he sat down, pushing Xu Youyu's fried noodles in front of her. "Diligently following Principal Wang's teaching to get more exercise."

"Didn't you consider any of the competition clubs?" Xu Youyu asked curiously. "I think Xixi joined the Math Club, right? Aren't you going to accompany her?"

"When she goes to the Math Club, she's soaring through the world of knowledge," Li Luo said, shaking his head. "If I went, it'd just be pure torture. Why would I ask for trouble?"

"Weren't your high school entrance exam scores quite good? Is it really that exaggerated?"

"I scored 110 on the entrance exam because that's the limit of my ability. Some people scored 120 because that was the maximum score on the paper. I'm very self-aware."

"Well, in that case," Xu Youyu smiled, suggesting while eating her fried noodles, "why not join the Literature Club?"

"Oh? So that's what you were waiting for." Li Luo raised his eyebrows, finally understanding Xu Youyu's preamble. "You're in the Literature Club too, Senior?"

"I'm the vice president."

"I thought you'd be the president."

"If you join the club," Xu Youyu said with a grin, "I might become the president very soon."

"Huh?" Li Luo was taken aback. "Don't tell me you and the other vice president have some kind of drama going on where whoever gets me to join becomes the president?"

"You wish." Xu Youyu rolled her eyes at him. "I was just being polite."

"Then forget it. The Literature Club sounds like too much trouble. For the Basketball Club, you can just go whenever you want, there aren't any strict requirements."

"The Literature Club doesn't have any strict requirements either."

"Didn't you say we have to submit one manuscript a month?"

"Guess who's the one collecting the manuscripts?" Xu Youyu chuckled. "If I recruit you, you'll be under my supervision. If you don't want to write, then don't."

"Is that even allowed?" Li Luo looked astonished. "Then what's the difference between me joining and not joining?"

"What if you feel like writing something later?" Xu Youyu said. "Besides, the Literature Club isn't just about writing manuscripts. We have club activities too, you know. It's just a matter of whether you want to participate."

"Like what?"

"Like..." Xu Youyu started to say, but then she fell silent for a moment.

It seemed the Literature Club didn't really have any interesting activities.

Clubs like the Math Club and Physics Club were purely competition-focused. The evening club activities were equivalent to an eighth period, where the competition teachers would prepare special lessons.

Clubs like the Basketball Club, Table Tennis Club, and Anime Club were more relaxed. Members could find companionship, play ball, or watch anime together.

As for the Literature Club, during the evening club activities, everyone would just gather in a designated activity room to chat, shoot the breeze, and share good books or articles they had recently read.

During the Pen Pal Club on Saturday afternoons, they would also critique each other's recent works.

Besides that, there was one other interesting thing.

"The Literature Club doesn't really have any interesting activities, but there's one thing I find quite fun," Xu Youyu said with a smile. "In the Literature Club, you can choose one or two pen pals."

"The two of you agree to communicate through letters, just like the scholars of the past."

"Some things might not be suitable to say when talking to friends face-to-face, but they can be conveyed through written correspondence."

Li Luo blinked and couldn't help but ask, "But can't you do that without joining the Literature Club?"

"But you might not find people willing to correspond with you through letters. There are more people in the Literature Club who are willing to do it," Xu Youyu coaxed. "Come on, come on. Once I become the president, I'll make you the vice president!"

"Heh, if you want to order me around, just say so. Forget about being vice president," Li Luo said with a pout. "Washing my clothes for a month would be more practical."

Xu Youyu: "...I think you're asking for a beating."

(End of Chapter)
